title: Glyph — Award-Style Portfolio Concept
tagline: A self-initiated, Awwwards-caliber personal portfolio build — kinetic type, GSAP scroll choreography, and a custom cursor system.
overview: Glyph is a self-initiated concept build — a fictional creative-director-and-frontend-architect persona used to demonstrate the highest bar of UI, motion, and engineering craft: kinetic typography, a GSAP-driven pinned horizontal gallery, scroll-scrubbed text reveals, and a custom magnetic cursor, built without a single generic hero-cards-stats-CTA layout.
problem: Most developer portfolios default to the same template pattern — hero, card grid, stats, testimonials, CTA — because it's fast to build. Prospective clients rarely see proof that a designer-developer can break that mold and still ship something performant and accessible.
solution: Designed and built an entirely bespoke single-page experience: eight visually distinct sections (no repeated layout twice), a pinned horizontal scroll gallery for selected work, a GSAP scroll-scrubbed manifesto, a split sticky-scroll process timeline with SVG path drawing, and a flagship case-study deep-dive reusing real photography from the Bright Smiles Dental build — all respecting prefers-reduced-motion and touch devices.
results: A live, fully working portfolio concept that proves range across creative direction, motion design, and Next.js/React frontend architecture — used as proof of capability for prospective clients who want a website that doesn't look like everyone else's.
